sourcedFrom: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 (2026)
cleanIntro:
HK's own strip for the VP9CC, the compact striker-fired 9 mm, in HK's order and no further: frame, slide, recoil spring assembly, barrel and magazine. No tools are needed, and neither is a trigger pull. Turning the disassembly lever down decocks the firing pin, and that lever will not turn until the magazine is out and the slide is locked back.

HK sets two intervals. Normal cleaning is after each firing or every 12 months, whichever comes first. Major cleaning, the deep clean here, is after 600 cartridges, or whenever the pistol has met sand, dust, water (saltwater especially) or other contamination you can see.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, finger off the trigger
steps.action: Point the muzzle where nobody could be hurt by an unintended shot, with your finger off the trigger and outside the guard. Put safety glasses on and turn the ejection port away from you.
steps.prose: The VP9CC has a trigger safety and internal safeties but no safety lever to set. Removing the magazine does not stop it firing a round that is in the chamber, so the clearing order is what makes it safe to handle.
steps.quote: Your VP9CC pistol does not have a conventional manual safety and it will fire if the trigger is pulled when there is a round in the chamber, even if the magazine is removed.
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 4, Firing, printed p.18; clearing step 1, printed p.20
steps.warn: To unload and clear your pistol, you MUST proceed in this order.

steps.title: Magazine out before the slide moves
steps.action: Hold a hand under the magazine, press the magazine catch on either side of the frame, and take the magazine out.
steps.prose: With the magazine gone, working the slide cannot feed another round. Racking first with the magazine still in does exactly that.
steps.quote: Hold your hand under the magazine. 2. Press magazine catch
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 4, Clearing and Safety Check Procedure, step 2, printed p.20

steps.title: Slide racked and locked back
steps.action: Grip the rear serrations and rack the slide back, watching the port for a round or an empty case. Push up and hold the slide release on either side, then let the slide come forward until the release catches it.
steps.prose: Confirm it is held on the release before you let go. The slide must also be locked here for the strip, so this step does two jobs.
steps.quote: lock the slide to the rear by allowing the slide to move forward until it engages the slide release.
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 4, Clearing and Safety Check Procedure, step 3, printed p.20

steps.title: Chamber and feed ramp, by eye and by finger
steps.action: Look into the chamber through the open port, then sweep the chamber and feed ramp with a finger. Take out any round or case you find. If a round stays in the chamber, go through the clearing procedure again; if it will not extract, HK sends you to a gunsmith.
steps.prose: The red mark on the extractor is a loaded chamber indicator, not a check: HK says never to rely on a mechanical device or on memory. Do not pry at a live round with a metal tool.
steps.quote: Physically inserting a finger through the ejection port and sweeping the chamber and feed ramp area.
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 4, Clearing and Safety Check Procedure, step 4, printed p.21
steps.warn: Do not use a metal tool to attempt to remove an unfired cartridge because it could ignite the primer and cause the cartridge to rupture

steps.title: Disassembly lever down to six o’clock
steps.action: Leave the slide locked back and the magazine out. Turn the disassembly lever, on the left side of the frame, down to about six o’clock.
steps.prose: If the lever will not move, do not force it: a magazine in the well or a slide that is not locked back blocks it. With the lever down the firing pin is decocked, which is why this pistol never asks for a trigger pull to come apart.
steps.quote: This prevents the need to pull the trigger in order to release the slide from the receiver.
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 5, Disassembly, step 2, printed p.22; disassembly safety, printed p.11
steps.warn: To ensure that your pistol is unloaded, disassembly MUST be performed in this order.

steps.title: Slide released and run forward off the frame
steps.action: Hold the slide, press the slide release down, and guide the slide forward off the front of the frame.
steps.prose: It leaves toward the muzzle. Keep hold of it the whole way: it starts forward from the locked-back position with the recoil spring behind it, and the barrel and spring come off with it.
steps.quote: Depress the slide release and push the slide forward, removing the slide from the top of the frame assembly
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 5, Disassembly, step 3, printed p.23

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly forward, then up
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down. Push the recoil spring assembly forward and lift it up, away from the barrel and slide.
steps.prose: Forward comes first, because the rear of the assembly is braced against the barrel. Before it comes out, note which end faces the muzzle and how its rear end sits centered on the barrel; HK shows an off-center spring as the wrong way to put it back.
steps.quote: carefully push the recoil spring assembly forward and upward, separating the recoil spring assembly from the barrel and slide
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 5, Disassembly, step 4, printed p.23
steps.warn: Components, such as springs, are under pressure and could cause serious injury.

steps.title: Barrel forward a little, then pressed out through the port
steps.action: Tip the barrel slightly forward and press up on its locking block through the ejection port until the barrel comes free of the slide.
steps.prose: The block is seated in the ejection port, which is what holds the barrel in. Pressing on the block frees it; pulling on the muzzle does not.
steps.quote: Pivot the barrel slightly forward and press upward on the barrel locking block through the ejection port, separating the barrel from the slide.
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 5, Disassembly, step 5, printed p.23

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have the slide, the barrel, the recoil spring assembly, the frame and the magazine: the five parts HK shows as the VP9CC taken down. The slide and frame come no further apart in this book. The magazine does, and it is the deep clean.
steps.prose: HK wants this much apart every time the pistol is cleaned. A rod run in from the muzzle with the slide only locked back leaves dirt and oil building up inside.
steps.quote: As with any semi-automatic pistol, your VP9CC should be disassembled into its major components every time it is cleaned.
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 6, Cleaning, printed p.30

steps.title: Bore brushed from the chamber end
steps.action: Wet a 9 mm bronze bore brush with cleaning solution and scrub from the chamber toward the muzzle, six passes or more. Patch the loosened fouling out. Scrub the outside of the barrel and the locking block with the wet nylon toothbrush and wipe both down.
steps.prose: Bronze is the brush HK lists for this polygonal bore. A steel one costs accuracy, and the damage does not come out.
steps.quote: scrub the bore from the chamber to the muzzle with at least six (6) passes.
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 6, Normal Cleaning, Barrel, printed p.31
steps.warn: Do not use a steel bore brush which can scratch the polygonal bore and reduce accuracy.

steps.title: Barrel and chamber: oiled after firing, dry before it
steps.action: After cleaning, oil the barrel and chamber with a quality gun lubricant. Before the pistol is next fired, take that oil back out of both with the cleaning kit.
steps.prose: HK’s maintenance plan lists the oil and the de-oil as two separate jobs. The oil protects the bore in storage; left there at the next shot, the excess counts as an obstruction.
steps.quote: If any obstruction is found, remove it – including any excess lubricants – before firing so that your pistol will function safely and correctly.
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 6, Cleaning, printed p.30; maintenance plan items 2–3, printed p.33

steps.title: Slide scrubbed inside, wiped, oiled
steps.action: Scrub the inside of the slide with the nylon toothbrush wet with cleaning solution, then lift the loose fouling with a rag and cotton swabs. Wipe the sights clean with a rag. Oil the slide, and oil its guideways before firing.
steps.prose: Work gently, with the barrel and spring out, so the breech face and the whole length of the guideways can be reached.
steps.quote: Gently scrub all internal surfaces of the slide using the nylon toothbrush moistened with cleaning solution.
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 6, Normal Cleaning, Slide, printed p.31; maintenance plan items 4–8, printed p.33

steps.title: Recoil spring cleaned as one assembly
steps.action: Clean off the fouling you can see with cleaning solution and a nylon toothbrush, or a rag and cotton swabs, then oil it.
steps.prose: HK cleans it whole and gives no procedure for taking it apart. Before firing, HK’s plan has you check both its function and its condition.
steps.quote: Remove all visible fouling using cleaning solution, a nylon toothbrush or a rag and cotton swabs.
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 6, Normal Cleaning, Recoil spring assembly, printed p.31; maintenance plan item 9, printed p.33

steps.title: Frame: where the slide rides and where the barrel unlocks
steps.action: Scrub the carbon off the frame gently with the wet nylon toothbrush, then lift it with a rag and cotton swabs. Oil the guide rails and the trigger mechanism after firing.
steps.prose: Two places get the attention: the area the slide covers, and the block the barrel works against as it unlocks.
steps.quote: Concentrate on the area normally covered by the slide and the unlock block area that interfaces with the barrel.
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 6, Normal Cleaning, Frame Assembly, printed p.31; maintenance plan items 10–12, printed p.33

steps.title: Top of the magazine
steps.action: With the magazine empty, scrub the follower and the feed lips gently with the wet nylon toothbrush, then wipe the whole magazine with a rag and cotton swabs.
steps.prose: The routine clean leaves it assembled. HK’s lubrication plan gives the magazine no oil.
steps.quote: Gently scrub the top of the magazine, concentrating on the follower and feed lips
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 6, Normal Cleaning, Magazine, printed p.31; maintenance plan items 17–18, printed p.34

steps.title: Look it over while it is apart
steps.action: Check for damaged or missing parts, cracks, burrs, dents, corrosion, parts that should move or spring and do not, looseness that was not there before, and too little lubricant.
steps.prose: Looseness is the one that needs a memory: it only means something against how the part felt when it was right.
steps.quote: During and after cleaning, visually inspect the pistol and its components for any irregularities that may cause problems or stoppages during operation.
steps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 6, Inspection, printed p.32

deepSteps.title: After 600 cartridges, or after grit or water
deepSteps.action: Major cleaning is normal cleaning plus two things: the magazine comes apart, and every part is rinsed or soaked in solution and scrubbed. Do the normal clean first. HK calls for this after 600 cartridges, and after sand, dust, water or any other dirt you can see.
deepSteps.prose: Water counts even when the pistol looks clean, and HK singles out saltwater.
deepSteps.quote: Performed after the firing of 600 cartridges or when the pistol is exposed to, or contaminated with:
deepSteps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 6, Cleaning Intervals and Major Cleaning, printed p.31

deepSteps.title: Magazine empty, floor plate slid forward
deepSteps.action: Glasses on, live ammunition off the bench, and every round out of the magazine. Push the locking plate in through the hole in the floor plate with a 6 mm (.25 in.) pin punch and slide the floor plate slightly forward.
deepSteps.prose: The locking plate is what stops the floor plate sliding, so push it in fully before you slide. Point the base of the magazine away from your own face and everyone else’s from here on.
deepSteps.quote: Using pin punch, push in magazine locking plate (A) and slide magazine floor plate forwards slightly (B)
deepSteps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 5, Magazine Disassembly, step 1, printed p.28
deepSteps.warn: Be aware of the force exerted by the magazine spring while removing and installing the magazine floorplate.

deepSteps.title: Floor plate off; locking plate, spring and follower out
deepSteps.action: Keep a thumb over the opening as you pull the floor plate off, let the spring up slowly, then take out the locking plate, the spring and the follower.
deepSteps.prose: Note which way the follower sits on the spring and the spring on the locking plate; HK’s assembly steps send you back to those positions. If you have 10- and 12-round magazines, do them one at a time so their parts cannot be swapped.
deepSteps.quote: Remove magazine locking plate, magazine spring and follower.
deepSteps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 5, Magazine Disassembly, steps 2–3, printed p.28
deepSteps.warn: Magazine springs and followers are optimized for their specific capacity. Ensure magazines are reassembled with the correct capacity-specific components.

deepSteps.title: Everything rinsed or soaked, and scrubbed
deepSteps.action: Rinse the parts with cleaning solution or immerse them in it, and scrub each one thoroughly with a nylon brush. Use a bottle brush inside the magazine housing and a rag on the outside, the follower and the spring.
deepSteps.prose: HK does not normally recommend an ultrasonic cleaner: it can strip the colored reference marks off the frame and the extractor, and the extractor’s red mark is the loaded chamber indicator.
deepSteps.quote: All parts should be rinsed with or immersed in cleaning solution and thoroughly scrubbed with a nylon brush.
deepSteps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 6, Major Cleaning, printed p.31; maintenance plan items 17–18, printed p.34
deepSteps.warn: Use of ultrasonic cleaning machines can result in the unwanted removal of colored reference markings of the frame assembly, extractor and control lever (where applicable).

deepSteps.title: Dried right through, then oiled again
deepSteps.action: Dry every part with compressed air, or with a rag and cotton swabs, with glasses on. Then oil the pistol again: the slide and its guideways, the recoil spring, the frame’s guide rails, the trigger mechanism and the barrel. The magazine goes back dry.
deepSteps.prose: The soak took off the oil the routine clean put on, so oiling is done again here. Dry comes first: solution trapped in the slide or frame thins whatever oil goes over it.
deepSteps.quote: All components should be thoroughly dried after being coated in cleaning solutions of any kind before reassembly
deepSteps.cite: VP9CC SERIES — OPERATOR'S MANUAL — May 2026, HKUSA 51001819 - 052026 — Section 6, Cleaning, printed p.30; Major Cleaning, printed p.31; maintenance plan, printed pp.33–34
deepSteps.warn: Exercise caution if using compressed air.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Bore: wet 9 mm bronze brush, chamber to muzzle, six passes or more
Patches until the loose fouling is out
Outside and locking block: wet nylon toothbrush, then rag and swabs
Barrel and chamber oiled after cleaning; oil removed again before firing

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Loose fouling off with rag and cotton swabs
Lube: the slide after cleaning, its guideways before firing

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING ASSEMBLY
tasks: Visible fouling off with solution and toothbrush, or rag and swabs
Function and condition checked before firing

cleaning.name: FRAME
tasks: Carbon off: the area under the slide and the unlock block
Loose fouling off with rag and cotton swabs
Lube: guide rails and trigger mechanism

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Empty: follower and feed lips with the wet toothbrush
Whole magazine wiped with rag and swabs

reassembly: Glasses on and the base of the magazine pointed away from faces. Follower onto the magazine spring, and the spring onto the locking plate, both in the positions they came out in.
⛔ Only this magazine’s own spring and follower: HK warns against a 10-round spring or follower in a larger magazine, because wrong parts may cause malfunctions.
Follower, spring and locking plate pressed into the housing. Hold the locking plate in and slide the floor plate on from the front until the plate catches in it; listen for the click.
Check the magazine: the follower slides up and down freely under spring force and rises nearly flush with the bottom of the feed lips. If not, take it apart and do it again.
Barrel into the slide, then pushed to the rear until it locks with the slide.

⛔ Recoil spring assembly into the slide the way round it came out, its rear end braced on the control surfaces on the barrel and the whole assembly centered. HK’s figure marks a spring sitting off to either side as wrong.
With no magazine in the well and the disassembly lever still down, set the slide assembly on the frame and pull it all the way back until the slide release can be pushed up to hold it there.
Turn the disassembly lever to the rear and let the slide go forward.
Function check before any live ammunition.
fncheck: HK calls this check essential after every reassembly. Clear the pistol again first, with the full clearing procedure. Rack the slide three or four times quickly, finger off the trigger and outside the guard: it should move freely under the recoil spring without binding or locking up. Let the slide forward. With the pistol EMPTY and pointed in a safe direction, pull the trigger and listen for a click. Keep the trigger held back, rack the slide and let it return to battery, then release the trigger and listen for the click of the reset. Insert an EMPTY magazine and rack the slide: it should lock back. Take the empty magazine out and make sure the pistol is clear. If any part of this gives trouble, HK asks you to call its Customer Service.
reassemblyRoutine: Barrel into the slide, then pushed to the rear until it locks with the slide.

⛔ Recoil spring assembly into the slide the way round it came out, its rear end braced on the control surfaces on the barrel and the whole assembly centered. HK’s figure marks a spring sitting off to either side as wrong.
With no magazine in the well and the disassembly lever still down, set the slide assembly on the frame and pull it all the way back until the slide release can be pushed up to hold it there.
Turn the disassembly lever to the rear and let the slide go forward.
Function check before any live ammunition.
